question.worked_solution:
First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta ={cosh}^{2}⁡\theta +{sinh}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =\frac{x}{3},$ we get

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\frac{2x}{3})={cosh}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+{sinh}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}({cosh}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+{sinh}^{2}⁡(\frac{x}{3}))\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\frac{2x}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\frac{2x}{3}))|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\frac{2\cdot 4}{3})-\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\frac{2\cdot 1}{3})) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(\,sinh\,(\frac{8}{3})-sinh\,(\frac{2}{3})).\end{aligned}
$$
